Other / User-Facing.text: Reactive Resume answers on `APP_URL` (`rxresu.me`) and an optional alias, `APP_ALIAS_URL` (`rx.cv`). Every public page works on both without a redirect: resume web pages, the short link `/<username>`, the home page and marketing pages, and the API they call. A link that works on one domain works on the other, so people never meet "works here but not there". Share shows and copies the alias, the shorter address.
- Alias redirects everything except `/<username>`: one address per page, but `rxresu.me/<username>` and `rx.cv/<username>/<slug>` would behave differently.
- Alias as the primary domain with 308s from `rxresu.me`: backlinks survive a 308, but `.cv` is a country-code domain search engines don't treat as generic, while `.me` is.

- **No demand evidence yet.** RX-79 is conditional on APP-08 (RX-77) showing that people apply on behalf of several clients. RX-77 shipped a limited pilot ([#3848](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/pull/3848)): one owner shares one resume version with one reviewer, optionally with read-only application progress. It has no usage yet. Agents cannot interview coaches, nonprofits or university services; that research needs the owner.

# Reactive Resume: job application improvements

Based on [HireSweep competitor research, October 30, 2026](../research/hiresweep-2026-10-30.md). Source-code findings refer to Reactive Resume 6.0.10 at commit `33920b2e856048f3c5951bddbc00ba9d29778f61`; recheck the current implementation before starting each item.

Connect Reactive Resume's existing resume, career, and application tools to the repetitive work of applying: capture a posting, reuse accurate answers, prepare the right documents, fill supported forms, and retain what was submitted.
- [ ] Support connecting the helper to a self-hosted Reactive Resume installation.

Set release thresholds after baseline measurement. Higher match scores and vendor feature counts are not substitutes for measured user benefit. Use voluntary research or opt-in measurement consistent with Reactive Resume's privacy commitments.
Tracked reference for coding agents working on Reactive Resume. Everything here is in git, so it exists in every
repository, in `~/Projects/reactive-resume-private/` on the maintainer's machine. Never commit them here.
Research date: October 30, 2026. Reactive Resume baseline: version 6.0.10, commit `33920b2e856048f3c5951bddbc00ba9d29778f61`.

HireSweep has added a meaningful application-execution layer around Reactive Resume: reusable form answers, browser-assisted applications, hosted application runs, and workflows for people applying on behalf of clients. Its resume builder, AI editing, job tracking, fit review, discovery, and API/MCP surfaces substantially overlap capabilities already present in Reactive Resume.

Reviewed HireSweep's homepage, pricing, three feature pages, recruiter landing page, comparison index, complete public documentation, public OpenAPI specification, public extension metadata, selected shipped JavaScript bundles, and Chrome Web Store listing. Compared them with Reactive Resume source for web, native mobile, API, schemas, database ownership, assistant tools, and scheduled discovery. Checked Simplify, Huntr, Teal, and LoopCV through their own product/help pages.

- **Observed:** public prices and policies; explicit source attribution; published extension listing; public API contracts; client-side interfaces shipped in public assets; Reactive Resume implementation inspected at the baseline above.

Hosted AI removes provider setup for new users. Its privacy policy identifies Anthropic Claude as its hosted AI and also describes personal provider keys. Reactive Resume already supports administrator-provided AI as well as personal connections; the difference is a turnkey funded service, not a missing model integration. Sources: [HireSweep AI](https://docs.hiresweep.com/guides/using-ai), [privacy policy](https://docs.hiresweep.com/legal/privacy-policy), [Reactive Resume shared AI implementation](../../../packages/api/src/features/ai-providers/service.ts).

Reactive Resume already schedules discovery, reads and verifies individual postings, canonicalizes URLs, suppresses duplicates, saves opportunities, and supports in-app and optional email notifications. Its discovery chips match preference phrases; they are not equivalent to a resume-based semantic ranking. Existing retrieval uses configurable web-access providers rather than HireSweep's documented directory/feed approach. This is a quality and onboarding opportunity, not a missing discovery feature. Evidence: [jobs](../../../packages/api/src/features/career/jobs.ts), [matching](../../../packages/api/src/features/career/matching.ts), [posting retrieval](../../../packages/api/src/features/applications/posting.ts).

Reactive Resume already offers copies linked to jobs and assistant-generated passage edits that the user accepts or rejects, on web and mobile. The separate `applications.ai.tailorResume` endpoint, exposed through MCP, rewrites only the professional summary and then links the new copy. Its MCP description accurately describes this limitation. Do not infer that the main web/mobile tailoring workflow is summary-only. Evidence: [web assistant](../../../apps/web/src/features/assistant/assistant-panel.tsx), [mobile assistant](../../../apps/mobile/src/features/assistant/assistant-screen.tsx), [proposed edits](../../../packages/api/src/features/agent/tools.ts), [API tailoring](../../../packages/api/src/features/applications/ai.ts), [MCP description](../../../packages/mcp/src/tool-meta.ts).

Reactive Resume has overlapping career preferences, facts, stories, application-specific answers, drafting/tightening, copy/download controls, and submitted snapshots. The inspected schema does not provide an equivalent structured application profile or user-wide question/answer library. Reusing career evidence is different from reusing a reviewed answer to a recurring form question. Evidence: [career schemas](../../../packages/schema/src/career.ts), [web Apply](../../../apps/web/src/features/career/workspace/apply.tsx), [mobile Apply](../../../apps/mobile/src/features/workspace/tabs/apply.tsx).

Reactive Resume's Apply workflow prepares and records answers; users submit on the employer's site. Its similarly named MCP `autofill_application_from_job` populates the internal application record from a posting. It is not employer-form autofill. No equivalent browser extension or hosted application execution was found in inspected source.

Reactive Resume's inspected resume, application, and career records are user-owned. Multiple resumes do not provide delegated access, client isolation, permissions, approvals, or shared reporting. A full agency module would be a new ownership model, not a small UI addition.
## What is already covered or stronger in Reactive Resume

| Capability                                 | HireSweep evidence                             | Current Reactive Resume baseline                                                           | Decision                                           |

Reactive Resume evidence: [template schema](../../../packages/schema/src/templates.ts), [career schema](../../../packages/schema/src/career.ts), [workspace](../../../apps/web/src/features/career/workspace), [native workspace](../../../apps/mobile/src/features/workspace), [ATS checker](../../../apps/web/src/features/ats-checker), [MCP](../../../packages/mcp/src), [career implementation guide](../../../docs/contributing/career-platform.mdx).

| Product  | Primary-source evidence                                                                                                                             | Implication for Reactive Resume                                                                                                            |

| Huntr    | Free Basic includes application autofill; paid advanced AI. Application Packets bundle a tailored resume, letter, and follow-up, with bulk creation | A coherent prepare-and-review flow can improve existing Reactive Resume features without autonomous submission                             |

Hosted application execution adds persistent browser infrastructure, page-specific maintenance, account/session handling, document uploads, captchas, ambiguous completion states, and recovery from failed or duplicated attempts. These costs continue after initial implementation and complicate Reactive Resume's lightweight self-hosting/deployment options.

Set release thresholds after collecting baseline results. Do not substitute vendor feature lists or higher match scores for user outcomes. Use voluntary research or opt-in local measurement consistent with Reactive Resume's privacy positioning.

HireSweep explicitly states that portions derive from Reactive Resume and reproduces its MIT notice. It identifies itself as proprietary software operated by ManuSoft Inc. This research establishes attribution is present; it makes no finding about complete license compliance or exact fork ancestry. Source: [license page](https://docs.hiresweep.com/legal/license).

The practical competitive lesson is workflow completion. Reactive Resume already has many of the underlying capabilities and a richer documented candidate-preparation system than this review found in HireSweep. The best native additions connect those capabilities to the repetitive work outside the editor: capture the posting, reuse reviewed answers, prepare the right documents, and help fill the form. Agency operations and unattended submission should earn their place through demand and operating economics.

- **Delete accounts from an authenticated browser session.** API keys and OAuth tokens can no longer delete an account; integrations and MCP clients direct the owner to account settings. Other authenticated API operations keep their existing authentication methods. [#3595](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/pull/3595)

- **Review your transcript before requesting feedback.** Record for up to two minutes or upload a nonempty WebM, MP4/M4A, MP3, WAV or Ogg file up to 2 MiB. Original and edited provider transcripts remain distinguishable and deletable. Raw recordings are not stored by the Reactive Resume server; successful transcription clears local audio unless you keep it for download, while failures allow retry. Browser dictation and typing provide alternatives where supported. [Voice controls](/guides/career-workspace-reference#voice).

- **Open resumes on HTTP installations without crashing.** Builder session IDs no longer depend on `crypto.randomUUID()` being available in a secure browser context. [#3573](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/pull/3573)

- **Keep numeric drafts finite and within bounds.** The shared number input keeps partial text local, supports multi-digit typing and persists only finite bounded values. It preserves sibling autosaves and accessible input-group focus styling instead of saving `NaN` or repeatedly clamping a half-entered value. [#3594](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/pull/3594)

- **Render text symbols instead of rejecting the whole PDF.** Characters such as ★ now resolve through Noto Sans Symbols 2 rather than becoming question marks and failing the text-loss check. Preview and download errors retain the text-loss cause and show an actionable explanation. [#3583](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/pull/3583)

- **Size Free-form pages to their content.** Each page keeps A4 width and grows to the measured content height, with an A4 minimum, instead of spilling onto extra pages. Free-form is directly available in the Paper selector; the old fixed length control is removed. [#3597](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/pull/3597)

- **Keep item headers from wrapping mid-word.** Forme is updated to 0.28.0 to correct wrapping in item headers, with regression coverage for location text. [#3588](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/pull/3588)

- **Keep resume-copy selection overlays positioned correctly.** Source-resume cards now provide the positioning context for their overlays. [8aee5b7a9](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/commit/8aee5b7a9)

- **Keep sessions through temporary failures.** Rate limits and network errors no longer masquerade as a logged-out session, preventing transient logout during session refresh and route loading. [#3575](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/pull/3575)

- **Prevent duplicate authentication submissions.** Auth forms disable pending submissions, username sign-in is rate-limited, and password changes can revoke other sessions. Existing short passwords remain usable while password inputs apply native length constraints. [#3589](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/pull/3589)

- **Discover MCP tools consistently and with less work.** The live tool list and server card share precomputed input/output schemas and annotations, avoiding schema conversion on every discovery request while retaining normal tool-call validation. [70399d779](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/commit/70399d779)

[8aee5b7a9](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/commit/8aee5b7a9)

- **A free ATS checker that never uploads your resume.** Drop a PDF on [rxresu.me/ats-checker](https://rxresu.me/ats-checker) and it opens the file the way a parser would, pulls the text out, and reports what survived: whether the file carries real text or a picture of one, whether a multi-column layout scrambles the reading order, and whether your name, email, phone, links and dates come through intact. Everything runs in your browser — the file is never uploaded, nothing is stored, and no account is needed. Paste a job description and it will also tell you which of the posting's terms already appear in your resume. [#3382](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/pull/3382)

- **A score you can actually audit.** The report gives one number from 0 to 100 across readability, layout, sections, contact details and dates — and shows its working. Every finding cites the text that triggered it and the page it sits on, and the report states how many checks ran and how many were honestly skipped rather than quietly counting them as passes. Employment gaps, writing style and length are reported as unscored tips; they never move the score. [#3382](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/pull/3382)

- **Resume analysis has been replaced by the ATS check.** The old AI-scored analysis is gone, along with its stored results, its `get_resume_analysis` MCP tool, and the `POST /ai/analyze-resume` endpoint. What replaces it is deterministic and evidence-backed, with an optional AI second opinion on your writing that deliberately returns no score of its own. Self-hosters: read the upgrade note below. [#3382](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/pull/3382)

- **Bold text finally looks bold.** Most resumes pair Regular with SemiBold, which rendered `<strong>` almost indistinguishably from body text. Bold now resolves to the font family's true Bold face, so emphasis reads as emphasis — existing resumes will export with visibly stronger bold text. Thanks to [@santhiprakash](https://github.com/santhiprakash). [e065a1082](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/commit/e065a1082)

- The right sidebar's **ATS Check** section now runs live checks against your resume as you type — missing dates, malformed links, prose stranded in a narrow sidebar — before you export anything. [#3382](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/pull/3382)

- **Run deep check** renders your current resume to a PDF in your browser and runs the full file check against those exact bytes, which is the same file a recruiter receives. [#3382](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/pull/3382)

- Once a report exists, you can ask your own AI provider to review the writing — weak phrasing, bullets that describe duties rather than outcomes, and where a rewrite would land better. It sends only the extracted text, never the PDF. [#3382](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/pull/3382)

- Section detection understands more of the headings people actually use, so conventional sections are recognized across a wider range of resumes. [#3382](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/pull/3382)
- Toasts no longer slide underneath dialogs and sheets. [#3382](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/pull/3382)

- Bold text now uses the font family's true Bold face. Most resumes store their typography as Regular plus SemiBold, which rendered `<strong>` almost indistinguishably from body text on faces like Open Sans; bold now resolves to the family's 700 weight where it has one, and to its heaviest bold-class face where it does not. Existing resumes will export with visibly stronger bold text. Thanks to [@santhiprakash](https://github.com/santhiprakash). - **No more Browserless / Chromium dependency.** From v5.1.0 onwards, you do **not** need to run a `printer`, Browserless, or headless Chrome service alongside Reactive Resume. PDF generation is now performed entirely in your browser via `@react-pdf/renderer`. The `BROWSERLESS_TOKEN`, `PRINTER_ENDPOINT`, `PRINTER_APP_URL`, and `FLAG_DEBUG_PRINTER` environment variables are no longer read and can be removed from your `.env`.

- **One-service deployment.** Self-hosted Compose files no longer need a `printer:` service block. The minimum stack is now just Reactive Resume + PostgreSQL (with optional S3-compatible storage and SMTP).

title: "Reactive Resume vs Adobe Express"
description: "Compare Reactive Resume and Adobe Express for resume templates, PDF export, visual editing, structured data, and self-hosting."

Adobe Express suits you when the resume sits inside broader document, image, and layout work. Reactive Resume keeps the content in resume-specific fields, with resume-focused exports and a choice of where the app runs.

Adobe Express has a resume maker inside a general creative editor. Reactive Resume only does resumes: it organizes sections such as experience and education, renders them in a template, and keeps the same data when you change layouts or create new versions.
| Consideration    | Reactive Resume                                                           | Adobe Express                                           |
## Where Reactive Resume is a better fit

Use Reactive Resume when work history and other sections should stay structured rather than sit on the page as arranged elements. That makes it easier to copy a resume for each job, switch templates, write a matching cover letter that reuses the resume's design, or keep a data backup next to your document exports. The [Downloading your resume](/guides/exporting-your-resume) guide covers PDF, DOCX, Markdown, and JSON.

Choose Adobe Express when broad creative editing, visual assets, or a general document canvas are central to the task. Choose Reactive Resume when the resume itself is the task and you want reusable structured fields, resume-specific controls, and several export formats.
## Reactive Resume limitations in this comparison

Reactive Resume has a smaller visual asset library and no general-purpose design canvas. It is the wrong tool for heavy image work, graphic composition, or producing many non-resume document types. Adobe Express fits those needs better.

title: "Reactive Resume vs Canva"
description: "Compare Reactive Resume and Canva for free resume creation, visual control, exports, data portability, and self-hosting."
Canva suits freeform visual composition and gives you a broad design library. Reactive Resume is built around structured resume fields, reusable resume data, and the option to self-host.

Both tools make resumes, but they start from different models. Canva is a general design product with resume templates among its design types. Reactive Resume is a resume editor: work history, education, skills, and other sections are stored as data, then rendered through the template you pick.
| Consideration    | Reactive Resume                                                                                        | Canva                                                           |

Reactive Resume supports PDF, DOCX, Markdown, and JSON exports; see [Downloading your resume](/guides/exporting-your-resume). Its JSON format holds the content and settings so you can reuse them in another Reactive Resume resume. Canva's resume builder is part of a wider design environment, which fits better when the resume needs custom graphics, brand elements, or a layout beyond resume-specific controls.
## Where Reactive Resume is a better fit

Choose Reactive Resume when the content should stay in recognizable resume fields and you expect to reuse it across versions. You can change between 18 templates without re-entering the underlying sections, adjust layout settings, and export in several document and data formats. Cover letters are their own documents that share the resume's design, and Check mode flags lines that applicant tracking systems may read poorly.

It also fits when you care about infrastructure. Reactive Resume is [MIT-licensed](/legal/license), its source is public, and you can deploy it yourself. The [self-hosting guide](/self-hosting/docker) covers the Docker path, and hosted use stays available if you would rather not run the service.

Use Canva if the resume is mainly a visual design project and you want a general canvas with a broad asset library. Use Reactive Resume if you want a dedicated resume workflow, portable resume data, and the option to run the software yourself.
## Reactive Resume limitations in this comparison

Reactive Resume has a narrower design canvas. It does not try to match Canva's general composition tools or its asset library. If your resume depends on custom illustrations, heavy image editing, or unusual page composition, Canva gives you more direct control.

Reactive Resume also exports PDF, DOCX, Markdown, and JSON; see [Downloading your resume](/guides/exporting-your-resume). Choose Overleaf if LaTeX source, community templates, or collaborative academic documents are central to how you work. Choose Reactive Resume if you want a focused visual resume builder and structured fields without a LaTeX editing workflow.

description: "Compare Reactive Resume and Resume.io by free PDF access, templates, writing tools, exports, open source, and self-hosting."

Resume.io is a commercial, guided builder with sample content and a template-focused workflow. Its documented free PDF allowance is narrower: the Vancouver template, alongside TXT export. ## Where Reactive Resume is a better fit

Reactive Resume fits when you want to pick from all 18 templates and export a designed document without a template tier in the way. Cover letters are separate documents with the same design and the same free downloads. The [Downloading your resume](/guides/exporting-your-resume) guide covers PDF, DOCX, Markdown, and JSON. You also get source access and self-hosting. Reactive Resume is [MIT-licensed](/legal/license), and its [Docker guide](/self-hosting/docker) documents the self-hosted route. Its optional AI integration lets you configure a provider if you want help, while ordinary editing does not depend on it.

Choose Resume.io if its guided content, sample resumes, hosted workflow, and Vancouver free-PDF option match how you want to write. Choose Reactive Resume if you want its included templates, several export formats, and no premium tier on the core resume workflow.

Reactive Resume publishes 32 agent skills for resume writing and the job search. They cover complete text drafts, importable resumes, evidence gathering, proofreading, career changes, academic CVs, fourteen role families, cover letters, LinkedIn profiles, portfolios, applications, interviews and offers. This guide explains how to install them and choose the right workflow.

| What it is                            | Instructions for a workflow                                     | Tools that read and change your Reactive Resume data                       | A chat panel beside your document in the editor |

| Where it runs                         | Your agent: Claude Code, the Claude apps, Codex, Cursor, others | Any MCP client                                                             | Reactive Resume                                 |

Skills work on their own: paste your resume or a job posting and you get text, a table or a JSON file back. When your agent is also connected to the MCP server, the skills use its tools to read your resumes and applications and, after you say yes, write changes back. The skills ask before using a Reactive Resume tool that sends your data to your AI provider, such as match scores, the AI-tailored summary and drafted letters.

The skills live in the [`plugins/reactive-resume/skills` folder](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/tree/main/plugins/reactive-resume/skills) of the Reactive Resume repository, one folder per skill. Install the collection or choose the skills you need. Each works independently; related skills can help with the next task when installed.

The Reactive Resume plugin installs all 32 skills and connects the [MCP server](/guides/using-the-mcp-server) in one step. Your agent asks you to sign in to Reactive Resume the first time a skill needs your data.

Reactive Resume doesn't include an AI model of its own. To use the assistant, AI imports, drafting and the other AI features, connect a provider such as OpenAI, Anthropic or Google Gemini. Everything else in the app works without AI.
- Know which model you want to use, such as `gpt-6-luna` or `claude-haiku-5-5`. Reactive Resume suggests a default for each provider, but your account may not have access to every model.

Select your name at the bottom of the sidebar to open **Settings**, then choose **AI**. You can also go to `https://rxresu.me/dashboard/settings/ai` directly. Self-hosted instances use their own address.

Pick your provider from the **Provider** list. Reactive Resume suggests its usual **Model**. Use **Get an API key** to open that provider's key settings, then paste your key into **API key**. Switching providers clears the typed key. Change the model if you want a different one.

Select **Save and test**. Reactive Resume saves the provider, then sends it a tiny request to check that the key, address and every model you configured work. If the test passes, the dialog closes and the provider is ready to use.

Leave either field empty to use the model above. A connection with one model therefore keeps working exactly as before, with the same key, provider and approval. Task models use that same connection; Reactive Resume never switches to another provider.

Your personal API key is encrypted on the Reactive Resume server with AES-256-GCM before it's saved, and it's never shown again. Settings only ever show the last four characters. When a feature needs the key, the server decrypts it just long enough to call your provider.

Requests go from the Reactive Resume server to the provider you chose, using your key. Each interactive action asks you to approve its provider, model and data before sending. Canceling keeps the task available. Changes to the destination while approval is open require another approval. Scheduled requests run only after you enable the schedule. The Reactive Resume REST API lets your own scripts, extensions and automations read and change your documents and job applications. You authenticate with an API key that you create in Settings. This guide walks you through creating a key, making your first request and revoking the key when you're done.
- You need a Reactive Resume account. The examples use the hosted instance at `https://rxresu.me`. If you self-host, replace it with your own address.
Reactive Resume shows the key only once. If you lose it, revoke it and create a new one.

Every endpoint, with its parameters, request body and responses, is listed in the **API Reference** tab of these docs. Your own instance also serves the machine-readable OpenAPI document at `/api/openapi/spec.json` (for example `https://rxresu.me/api/openapi/spec.json`). | PDF, JSON Resume, Reactive Resume v4/current, LinkedIn imports                          | `POST /resumes/file-imports`                                                     |

File imports accept a multipart form. The format is one of `PDF`, `REACTIVE_RESUME`, `REACTIVE_RESUME_V4`, `JSON_RESUME` or `LINKEDIN`; the maximum file size is 10 MiB. PDF imports read the text layer without AI. AI-assisted PDF and Word parsing remain available under `/ai/pdf-parses` and `/ai/docx-parses`; save the resulting data through `/resumes/imports`.
curl "https://rxresu.me/api/openapi/resumes/file-imports" \

OAuth clients must send `resource=<instance origin>` (for example `resource=https://rxresu.me`) on authorization, token exchange and refresh requests. Discover the exact resource at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`. Authorization without `resource` is refused with `invalid_target` before sign-in. The error goes to the client's redirect address when the client is enabled and the address exactly matches its registration; otherwise the server answers `400` directly. Guest accounts must create an account before connecting.

- **When a reply fails**, your message is kept. Select **Retry**. **Switch model** appears when the provider caused the failure, such as a rejected key, a missing model or a rate limit. A lost internet connection says **Couldn't reach Reactive Resume** instead.

Reactive Resume runs a [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server, so AI clients such as Claude, Cursor and Codex can read and edit your resumes, cover letters and job applications when you ask them to in plain language. This guide shows you how to connect a client and lists everything the server offers.

The server address is your instance's address followed by `/mcp`. On the hosted instance it's `https://rxresu.me/mcp`. You can copy it from **Settings** → **Developer**, in the **MCP server** section.

Reactive Resume does not sell AI credits or run a model for you. # DeepSeek Harness Plugin for Reactive Resume — Design
**Package:** `dsh-plugin-reactive-resume`

Distribute a DeepSeek Harness plugin that connects Harness to a Reactive Resume account, so a DSH user can read, create, and edit resumes and job applications from their agent session with one config row and an API key.
### What Reactive Resume already ships
Reactive Resume exposes a complete remote MCP server. Nothing on the server side needs to change for this plugin to work.

`dsh-mcp-client` has no tool filtering and no way to contribute prompt text. A user pasting a raw MCP row into `cordis.yml` gets all 33 tool schemas in their context budget and no guidance on Reactive Resume's JSON Patch semantics. Those two things are the plugin's reason to exist.

| Scope            | Thin MCP bridge + prompt section                 | The tool layer already exists and is maintained in Reactive Resume. Reimplementing 33 tool contracts against oRPC would drift every release.                                                                                                                                                                    |

| Repo             | Standalone, outside the Reactive Resume monorepo | The plugin imports nothing from Reactive Resume — it speaks HTTP. The monorepo has no npm publish pipeline: root and every package are `private: true`, there is no build output, no changesets, no `NPM_TOKEN`, and no publish workflow. Adding one to ship a dependency-free package is cost without benefit. |

| Auth             | `x-api-key` only                                 | Two clicks in Reactive Resume settings. OAuth needs a token store and an interactive flow for no gain.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

# dsh-plugin-reactive-resume Implementation Plan

**Goal:** Ship an npm-distributed DeepSeek Harness plugin that connects a Harness session to a Reactive Resume account through the existing `/mcp` endpoint, curates the tool surface, and teaches the model Reactive Resume's JSON Patch semantics.

# Reactive Resume

Resume and job-search help for your AI agent, built around [Reactive Resume](https://rxresu.me), the free and open-source resume builder. The plugin bundles 32 skills and the Reactive Resume MCP server. Write from pasted text, build a resume for your profession, or connect your account to read and edit resumes, cover letters and applications.

The plugin connects to `https://rxresu.me/mcp`. The first time a skill needs your data, your agent asks you to sign in to Reactive Resume and approve access; no API key is stored in the plugin. Without signing in, the skills still work on text you paste.

Your agent's provider processes the text you give it under its own terms. Connected tools read and save data in your Reactive Resume account under its [privacy policy](https://docs.rxresu.me/legal/privacy-policy). Tools that use AI (match scores, tailored summaries, drafted messages) also send data to the AI provider you configured in Reactive Resume; the skills ask before calling them. They do not upload your resume to outside scanners or publish private work samples without authorization.
Self-hosting Reactive Resume? Install the skills on their own and connect your own server instead: `npx add-mcp <your-app-url>/mcp --name reactive-resume`.

Builds a story bank in Situation/Task/Action/Result/Reflection form mapped to the competencies the role and company test (such as Amazon's Leadership Principles), writes a cited company and role brief from public sources, predicts questions per round, drafts opener, why-us, weakness and salary answers, prepares questions to ask and a logistics checklist, and runs a post-interview debrief. Prepare the user for one specific interview using only their real experience. The deliverable is a **prep pack**: what the round scores, stories mapped to those competencies, a cited brief on the company and role, likely questions with a story for each, opening answers, questions to ask and a logistics checklist. After the interview, run a debrief that feeds the next round. Everything works in plain conversation; when the Reactive Resume MCP server is connected, read the application from it and save stories, questions and the debrief back.

Store each story once in five parts (Situation, Task, Action, Result, Reflection) and render it in whatever shape a question needs. Reflection answers the standard closing probe, "what would you do differently?", and turns a failure into evidence of growth. The same five fields are what Reactive Resume stores for a story.

**Cover the competencies.** Build a matrix of competencies (rows) against stories (columns). Aim for at least 2 stories per must-have competency and at least one each of: a failure or mistake, a conflict, leading without authority, ambiguity or prioritisation, a result the user drove, learning something fast, and customer focus. Senior candidates add hiring or developing others, a strategic bet and cross-organisation influence. Keep no more than half the stories from one project, at least 2 from the last 18 months, and at least one with a bad outcome. Size the bank by coverage, not a fixed count. An empty row becomes a question to the user, never an invented story. Without MCP, deliver the cards as Markdown the user can keep (Reactive Resume users can paste them into Career → Knowledge → Stories).

description: Advises what belongs on a resume or CV, what to omit, section order, length, gaps, personal details, and country or industry conventions. Audits existing content without a specific posting. Use for questions about photos, GPA, dates of birth, summaries or career situations. Use resume-writer or a role skill for a new text draft, resume-proofreader for editorial cleanup, resume-bullet-writer for bullets, resume-tailor for one posting and resume-builder for JSON. Works from pasted text or Reactive Resume MCP.
- With the Reactive Resume MCP server, follow [With Reactive Resume MCP](#with-reactive-resume-mcp); it also reads what the user already recorded in the app's Career profile.

- In Reactive Resume data, items with `hidden: true` don't print, and neither do `metadata.notes`. They are not hidden text and need no action; skip hidden items in every check. Hidden text means text that prints but can't be seen: compare `metadata.design.colors.text` with `background`, and scan `metadata.styleRules`, `metadata.stylesheet` and description HTML for colour, size or display tricks.
## With Reactive Resume MCP
Skip this section when the Reactive Resume MCP server isn't connected.

- **Imported resumes:** if a resume the user brings contains text that looks hidden (a keyword block matching the background colour, near-zero font size, text placed off the page, or a pasted list of the JD's terms with no context), flag it and offer to remove it. In Reactive Resume, an item with `hidden: true` is simply not rendered; that is not injection.
Reactive Resume's `score_application_match` is an LLM opinion that varies by model. Use its gap list; don't chase the number.

- Reactive Resume assistant and coach rules: never invent metrics, ownership, dates or qualifications; ask instead.
# Reactive Resume MCP recipes

Tool sequences and JSON Patch recipes for tailoring inside Reactive Resume. Use only when the Reactive Resume MCP server is connected. Read before writing, show the user a before/after, and get a yes before every change. Tool input names for `api_*` tools are generated from the app's API; confirm them with `tools/list` if a call is rejected.

description: Tailors one resume to one specific job posting. Builds a must-have/nice-to-have requirement table, an evidence map, gap questions instead of invention, a tailored copy (headline, summary, bullet order, skills), honest ATS guidance, and an optional cover letter for that posting. Use when the user says "tailor my resume to this job", "customize my CV for this posting", "match my resume to this job description", "what keywords am I missing", "make my resume ATS-friendly for this role", "will this get past the ATS", "the job asks for X and I don't have it", or pastes a job ad with a resume. Works from pasted text; uses Reactive Resume MCP tools when connected. Not for bullets with no target job (resume-bullet-writer), what belongs on a resume or a general audit (resume-content-guide), tracking or follow-ups (job-application-manager), or interview prep and practice (interview-prep, mock-interview).
2. The base resume (pasted text, a file, or a Reactive Resume record).

Repository & Build Metadata.text:
"description": "Reactive Resume is a free and open-source resume builder for writing resumes and cover letters, checking your work, and tracking job applications.

### Features

- Real-time preview while you edit, with more than a dozen templates and full control over fonts, colors and layout
- Export to PDF, DOCX and OpenDocument, or share a public link
- Cover letters and a job application tracker alongside your resumes
- Import from JSON Resume, LinkedIn and earlier Reactive Resume versions
- Optional AI assistant with your own provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama and more)
- Passkeys, two-factor authentication and single sign-on with Cloudron
- Translated into more than 50 languages
- No tracking or ads; your data stays on your server
",

```
cloudron env set --app $CLOUDRON-APP-FQDN FLAG_DISABLE_SIGNUPS=true
```
",

"description": "Reactive Resume is a free and open-source resume builder for writing resumes and cover letters, checking your work, and tracking job applications.

### Features

- Real-time preview while you edit, with more than a dozen templates and full control over fonts, colors and layout
- Export to PDF, DOCX and OpenDocument, or share a public link
- Cover letters and a job application tracker alongside your resumes
- Import from JSON Resume, LinkedIn and earlier Reactive Resume versions
- Optional AI assistant with your own provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama and more)
- Passkeys, two-factor authentication and single sign-on with Cloudron
- Translated into more than 50 languages
- No tracking or ads; your data stays on your server
",

Import/Export Format Compatibility.text: Reactive Resume exports PDF, DOCX, Markdown, and JSON, and it supports authenticated automation through its API and MCP server. Its public [ATS checker](/guides/using-the-ats-checker) scores how faithfully software can extract your PDF, shows the text as software reads it, and lists which of a posting's terms already appear in it. Inside the editor, [Check mode](/guides/checking-your-resume) runs the same kind of checks live as you type, pins each issue to its line on the page, and matches your resume against the posting saved with a job application. Neither reports a match rate or predicts a rejection, because neither is knowable from the file.

Choosing **Default** there uses your current interface language, even if you chose another language earlier. Your source file and existing resumes remain unchanged.
